questions.title: Schistosoma has separate sexes
questions.question: Which one of the following trematodes has separate sex?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes, like most trematodes, is hermaphroditic, with both male and female reproductive organs in the same worm.
explanations.B: Correct. Schistosoma is the classic exception among trematodes: it has separate sexes (is dioecious), with the male and female worms pairing together in copula for their entire adult lives, the female residing in the male's gynaecophoric canal. This dioecious pattern distinguishes Schistosoma from essentially all other medically important trematodes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fasciola, like most trematodes, is hermaphroditic.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paragonimus westermani, like most trematodes, is hermaphroditic.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Schistosoma as the trematode with separate sexes, against the hermaphroditic pattern of the other trematodes covered in this chapter.

questions.title: Fasciola inhabits the large bile ducts
questions.question: Which of the following trematodes inhabit the large bile ducts?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes lives in the small intestine, not the bile ducts.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma species live in venous plexuses (mesenteric or vesical veins), not the bile ducts.
explanations.C: Correct. Fasciola (both F. hepatica and F. gigantica) is the classic liver fluke, living as an adult in the large bile ducts of the liver. Migrating juvenile flukes first tunnel through the liver parenchyma before settling in the bile ducts, where they cause obstruction and inflammation. This bile-duct habitat is what distinguishes Fasciola from the intestinal and vascular habitats of the other trematodes listed.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paragonimus westermani lives in the lungs, not the bile ducts.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Fasciola as the trematode inhabiting the large bile ducts.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Fasciola transmission is by ingesting metacercariae on plants
questions.question: Mode of transmission of Fasciola is by?

options.A: Ingestion of undercooked crabs harboring metacercaria
options.B: Ingestion of metacercaria found in plants
options.C: Ingestion of metacercaria found in undercooked fish
options.D: Penetration of the skin by furcocercus cercaria

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ingesting undercooked crabs or crayfish harbouring metacercariae is the transmission route for Paragonimus westermani (lung fluke), not Fasciola.
explanations.B: Correct. Fasciola is transmitted by ingesting metacercariae encysted on aquatic vegetation, such as watercress or other water plants eaten raw. This plant-borne route distinguishes Fasciola from the animal-flesh-borne routes of the other liver/lung/intestinal flukes and from Schistosoma's skin-penetration route.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ingesting metacercariae in undercooked fish is the transmission route for fish-borne flukes such as Heterophyes heterophyes and Clonorchis sinensis, not Fasciola.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Skin penetration by a furcocercous cercaria is the transmission route for Schistosoma species, not Fasciola, whose cercariae instead encyst on vegetation before ingestion.

questions.learning_objective: State that Fasciola is transmitted by ingesting metacercariae encysted on aquatic vegetation.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Heterophyes heterophyes is the smallest human trematode
questions.question: The smallest parasitic trematode infecting human is?

explanations.A: Correct. Heterophyes heterophyes is the smallest trematode that parasitizes humans, measuring only about 1 to 1.7 mm in length. Its tiny size does not limit its clinical importance: heavy intestinal infections can still cause diarrhoea and abdominal pain, and its eggs can occasionally embolise to the heart or brain.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma adult worms measure roughly 1 to 2 cm, considerably larger than Heterophyes heterophyes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Fasciola adults measure several centimetres, among the largest trematodes infecting humans, not the smallest.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paragonimus westermani adults measure roughly 1 cm, larger than the sub-2 mm Heterophyes heterophyes.

questions.learning_objective: State that Heterophyes heterophyes is the smallest trematode parasitizing humans.

questions.title: Biomphalaria snail is Schistosoma mansoni's intermediate host
questions.question: The biomphelaria snail is the intermediate host of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola's intermediate host is a Lymnaea snail, not Biomphalaria.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma haematobium's intermediate host is a Bulinus snail, not Biomphalaria.
explanations.C: Correct. The Biomphalaria snail, in Egypt specifically Biomphalaria alexandrina, is the intermediate host of Schistosoma mansoni. Miracidia hatching from eggs passed in stool penetrate this snail, develop through sporocyst generations, and release cercariae that go on to infect humans by skin penetration.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes' first intermediate host is a Pirenella (or Cerithidia) snail, not Biomphalaria.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the Biomphalaria snail as the intermediate host of Schistosoma mansoni.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Bulinus snail is Schistosoma haematobium's intermediate host
questions.question: The bolinus snail is the intermediate host of?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola's intermediate host is a Lymnaea snail, not Bulinus.
explanations.B: Correct. The Bulinus snail, specifically Bulinus truncatus in Egypt, is the intermediate host of Schistosoma haematobium. Miracidia penetrate this snail and, after asexual multiplication, release the cercariae that infect humans by skin penetration.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Schistosoma mansoni's intermediate host is a Biomphalaria snail, not Bulinus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes' first intermediate host is a Pirenella snail, not Bulinus.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the Bulinus snail as the intermediate host of Schistosoma haematobium.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Lymnaea snail is Fasciola's intermediate host
questions.question: The lymnea snail is the first intermediate host of?

explanations.A: Correct. The Lymnaea snail is the first (and only) intermediate host of Fasciola. Miracidia hatching from eggs passed in faeces penetrate this snail, and cercariae released from it encyst on aquatic vegetation as the infective metacercariae.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma haematobium's intermediate host is a Bulinus snail, not Lymnaea.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Schistosoma mansoni's intermediate host is a Biomphalaria snail, not Lymnaea.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes' first intermediate host is a Pirenella snail, not Lymnaea.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the Lymnaea snail as the intermediate host of Fasciola.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Schistosoma mansoni eggs have a lateral spine
questions.question: Which one of the following trematode eggs has a lateral spine?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola eggs are large, operculate and yellow-brown, without a spine of any kind.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma haematobium eggs carry a terminal spine, not a lateral one.
explanations.C: Correct. Schistosoma mansoni eggs are non-operculate and characteristically carry a lateral spine. This is a feature used to distinguish them microscopically from Schistosoma haematobium eggs, which instead carry a terminal spine. Neither species' eggs have the lid-like operculum seen in most other trematode eggs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes eggs are small and operculate, without a spine.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Schistosoma mansoni as the trematode whose egg carries a lateral spine, against Schistosoma haematobium's terminal spine.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Trematodes are leaf-shaped worms
questions.question: Trematodes are?

explanations.A: Correct. Trematodes (flukes) are characteristically leaf-shaped -- dorsoventrally flattened, oval to elongate bodies that give the group its common name, "flukes." This flattened, leaf-like body plan is a basic morphological feature used to recognise trematodes at a glance. It holds across the whole trematode group covered in this chapter, from the small Heterophyes heterophyes to the much larger Fasciola.
explanations.B: Incorrect. "Rounded worms" describes the nematodes (roundworms), a separate helminth group with a cylindrical, unsegmented body, not the trematodes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. "Tape-like worms" describes the cestodes (tapeworms), whose flattened but ribbon-like, segmented body differs from the trematodes' unsegmented, leaf-shaped one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trematodes are unsegmented; a segmented body plan (proglottids) is instead characteristic of the cestodes.

questions.learning_objective: State that trematodes are leaf-shaped, dorsoventrally flattened worms, distinguishing them from the rounded nematodes and segmented cestodes.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Heterophyes heterophyes inhabits the small intestine
questions.question: Which one of the following trematodes inhabit the small intestine?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola's adult habitat is the large bile ducts of the liver, not the small intestine.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma haematobium's adult habitat is the venous plexus of the urinary bladder, not the small intestine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Schistosoma mansoni's adult habitat is the venules of the large intestine, not the small intestine.
explanations.D: Correct. Heterophyes heterophyes is a small intestinal fluke: the adult worms attach to and live within the mucosa of the small intestine. Heavy infections can cause diarrhoea and abdominal pain as a result. This intestinal habitat contrasts with the bile-duct and venous-plexus habitats of the other trematodes listed.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Heterophyes heterophyes as the trematode inhabiting the small intestine.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Schistosoma transmitted by skin penetration
questions.question: Mode of transmission of Schistosoma species is by?

options.A: Ingestion of undercooked crabs harboring metacercaria
options.B: Ingestion of metacercaria found in plants
options.C: Ingestion of metacercaria found in undercooked fish
options.D: Penetration of the skin by furcocercus cercaria

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ingesting undercooked crabs harbouring metacercariae is the transmission route for Paragonimus westermani, not Schistosoma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Ingesting metacercariae found on plants is the transmission route for Fasciola, not Schistosoma.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ingesting metacercariae in undercooked fish is the transmission route for fish-borne flukes such as Heterophyes heterophyes, not Schistosoma.
explanations.D: Correct. Schistosoma species are transmitted by direct penetration of intact human skin by the free-swimming, fork-tailed (furcocercous) cercaria released from the snail intermediate host. This skin-penetration route is unique among the trematodes covered in this bank, all of which are otherwise acquired by ingestion.

questions.learning_objective: State that Schistosoma is transmitted by skin penetration of the furcocercous cercaria.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Pirenella conica is Heterophyes heterophyes' first intermediate host
questions.question: First intermediate host of Hetrophys hetrophys is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Lymnaea snail is Fasciola's intermediate host, not Heterophyes heterophyes'.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Biomphalaria alexandrina is Schistosoma mansoni's intermediate host, not Heterophyes heterophyes'.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bulinus truncatus is Schistosoma haematobium's intermediate host, not Heterophyes heterophyes'.
explanations.D: Correct. Pirenella conica, a brackish-water snail, is the first intermediate host of Heterophyes heterophyes. Cercariae released from this snail then encyst as metacercariae in a brackish-water fish (classically mullet), the second intermediate host, before humans become infected by eating the fish.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Pirenella conica as the first intermediate host of Heterophyes heterophyes.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p99

questions.title: Diagnostic stage of Schistosoma haematobium is the egg
questions.question: Diagnostic stage of schistosoma haematobium is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The miracidium is the stage that hatches from the egg in fresh water to infect the snail, not the stage recovered for diagnosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The furcocercous cercaria is the free-swimming, skin-penetrating stage released from the snail, not the diagnostic stage recovered from the patient.
explanations.C: Correct. The diagnostic stage of Schistosoma haematobium is the characteristic terminal-spined egg. It is recovered by microscopic examination of urine, classically a terminal urine sample collected around midday, when egg excretion peaks. This urine-based diagnosis distinguishes Schistosoma haematobium from Schistosoma mansoni, whose eggs are instead recovered from stool.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A leptocercous cercaria is not a Schistosoma stage at all; it is the simple-tailed cercarial type of Fasciola-group flukes.

questions.learning_objective: State that the egg, recovered from urine, is the diagnostic stage of Schistosoma haematobium.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Fasciola infective stage is encysted metacercaria
questions.question: Infective stage of Fasciola is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. "Existed metacercaria" is not a recognised parasitic stage; the infective stage is specifically the encysted form of the metacercaria.
explanations.B: Correct. The infective stage of Fasciola for humans is the encysted metacercaria, typically found attached to aquatic vegetation. Ingesting this stage on raw or undercooked water plants transmits the infection.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The miracidium is the stage that hatches from the egg to infect the snail intermediate host, not the human-infective stage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The egg is the stage passed in the definitive host's faeces; it must first hatch and develop through the snail before reaching the human-infective metacercarial stage.

questions.learning_objective: State that the encysted metacercaria is the infective stage of Fasciola for humans.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Heteroxenous parasite needs more than one host
questions.question: A heteroxenous parasite?

options.A: Lives in 2 different habitats in the body
options.B: Is found in an unusual host
options.D: Lives in one habitat in the body

explanations.A: Incorrect. Living in two different habitats within the body describes a heterotopic pattern, not the host-count-based definition of heteroxenous.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Being found in an unusual host describes an incidental (accidental) parasite, an unrelated category.
explanations.C: Correct. A heteroxenous parasite is one that requires more than one host -- typically an intermediate host in addition to the definitive host -- to complete its life cycle. Most trematodes and cestodes covered in this bank are heteroxenous, needing at least a snail intermediate host.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Living in one habitat in the body does not describe the host-count-based heteroxenous/monoxenous distinction.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Since option C correctly defines a heteroxenous parasite, "none of the above" is wrong.

questions.learning_objective: Define a heteroxenous parasite as one requiring more than one host to complete its life cycle.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Leptocercous cercaria has a simple tail
questions.question: Cercaria with simple tail is?

explanations.A: Correct. Leptocercous names a cercaria with a simple, unforked tail, the type produced by Fasciola-group flukes. This contrasts with the forked-tail furcocercous cercaria of Schistosoma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Furcocercous describes a forked-tail cercaria, the type produced by Schistosoma, not a simple-tailed one.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Microcercous describes a cercaria with a very short, stub-like tail, not a simple full-length one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Cercariaium" is not a recognised cercarial tail-type term.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Lophocercous describes a cercaria with a finned tail, the type associated with Heterophyes-group flukes, not a simple one.

questions.learning_objective: Define leptocercous as a simple, unforked cercarial tail type, produced by Fasciola-group flukes.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Miracidium is infective for the snail
questions.question: In the life cycle of hermaphroditic flukes, the infective stage for the snail is which of the following?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The cercaria is the stage released from the snail, infective for the next host (human or a second intermediate host), not the stage that infects the snail itself.
explanations.B: Correct. The miracidium, hatching from the egg in water, is the stage infective for the snail intermediate host. It actively penetrates the snail's tissues and develops through further larval stages inside it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The metacercaria is the encysted stage infective for the definitive host (or, for Schistosoma, the free cercaria is directly infective), not for the snail.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The redia is a larval stage that develops inside the snail, produced from the sporocyst, not the stage that initially infects it.
explanations.E: Incorrect. The sporocyst, like the redia, is a larval stage that develops inside the snail after miracidial penetration, not the stage that initially infects it.

questions.learning_objective: State that the miracidium is the stage infective for the snail intermediate host.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Trematoda needs a mollusc intermediate host
questions.question: Which class of helminthes needs a mollusc intermediate host for completing their life cycles?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Most medically important nematodes (roundworms) do not require a mollusc intermediate host; many have direct life cycles or use arthropod/other intermediate hosts.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The medically important cestodes (tapeworms) covered in this course use hosts such as pigs, cattle, copepods and fish as intermediate hosts, not molluscs.
explanations.C: Correct. Trematoda (flukes) is the helminth class that characteristically requires a mollusc -- specifically a snail -- as an intermediate host to complete its life cycle. This mollusc dependency is a feature shared by every trematode covered in this chapter. The medically important nematodes and cestodes taught alongside them instead use non-mollusc intermediate hosts, or none at all.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Since nematodes and cestodes do not generally require a mollusc intermediate host, "all of the above" is wrong.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Since cestodes do not generally require a mollusc intermediate host, this pairing incorrectly extends the mollusc requirement to cestoda as well.

questions.learning_objective: State that Trematoda, among the major helminth classes, requires a mollusc intermediate host.

questions.title: Fasciola gigantica habitat is the large bile ducts
questions.question: The habitat of Fasciola gigantica is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The jejunum and upper ileum are the habitat of intestinal worms such as Taenia solium, not Fasciola gigantica.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The large intestine is not Fasciola gigantica's habitat.
explanations.C: Correct. Fasciola gigantica, like Fasciola hepatica, is a liver fluke that lives as an adult in the large bile ducts. It reaches this site after a period of migration through the liver parenchyma as an immature fluke. This bile-duct habitat is the basis of the biliary obstruction and cholangitis seen in fascioliasis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Fasciola gigantica migrates through, but does not permanently reside in, liver cells -- its adult habitat is the bile ducts.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Muscle is not a habitat of Fasciola gigantica.

questions.learning_objective: State that Fasciola gigantica's habitat is the large bile ducts of the liver.

questions.title: Heterophyes heterophyes has a genital sucker
questions.question: A genital sucker is found in?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola hepatica has the standard oral and ventral suckers of a trematode, without an additional genital sucker.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Schistosoma mansoni has oral and ventral suckers, without an additional genital sucker.
explanations.C: Correct. Heterophyes heterophyes, a member of the family Heterophyidae, possesses a distinctive third sucker: the genital sucker (gonotyl). It sits near the ventral sucker, in addition to the usual oral and ventral suckers of a trematode. This extra sucker is a family-level feature not shared by Fasciola or Schistosoma species.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Schistosoma haematobium has oral and ventral suckers, without an additional genital sucker.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Fasciola gigantica has the standard oral and ventral suckers of a trematode, without an additional genital sucker.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Heterophyes heterophyes as the trematode possessing a genital sucker (gonotyl).

questions.title: S. haematobium lacks significant reservoir hosts
questions.question: The following about Schistosoma haematobium is correct EXCEPT?

options.C: Bulinus truncatus is the intermediate host
options.E: Diagnosed by detection of characteristic eggs in urine

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Schistosoma haematobium does cause urinary schistosomiasis.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Bladder cancer (squamous cell carcinoma) is a recognised long-term complication of chronic Schistosoma haematobium infection.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Bulinus truncatus is indeed Schistosoma haematobium's intermediate host.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the false statement, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Unlike species such as Schistosoma japonicum, which have important animal reservoir hosts, Schistosoma haematobium's definitive host is essentially humans alone, without a significant animal reservoir maintaining transmission.
explanations.E: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Schistosoma haematobium is indeed diagnosed by detecting its characteristic terminal-spined eggs in urine.

questions.learning_objective: State that Schistosoma haematobium lacks significant animal reservoir hosts, unlike zoonotic Schistosoma species such as S. japonicum.

questions.title: Schistosoma is the hermaphroditism exception
questions.question: All trematodes are hermaphrodite EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Fasciola gigantica is hermaphroditic, like most trematodes.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Heterophyes heterophyes is hermaphroditic, like most trematodes.
explanations.C: Correct. This is the exception, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Schistosoma has separate sexes rather than being hermaphroditic; the male and female worms pair together in copula for the duration of adult life, a pattern unique among the medically important trematodes covered in this bank.
explanations.D: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Fasciola hepatica is hermaphroditic, like most trematodes.

questions.title: Monoxenous parasite needs one host
questions.question: Monoxenous parasite?

options.A: Needs 2 hosts in the life cycle
options.B: Needs 1 host in the life cycle
options.C: Needs no host in the life cycle
options.D: Needs 3 hosts in the life cycle

explanations.A: Incorrect. Needing two hosts describes a heteroxenous parasite (with one intermediate host), not a monoxenous one.
explanations.B: Correct. A monoxenous parasite completes its entire life cycle within a single host, without requiring any intermediate host. This is the direct opposite of a heteroxenous parasite, which needs more than one host.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Every parasite needs at least one host; needing none would mean it is not a parasite at all.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Needing three hosts would describe an unusually complex heteroxenous life cycle, not a monoxenous one.

questions.learning_objective: Define a monoxenous parasite as one completing its life cycle in a single host.

field_notes.keySource: printed plain-text ANSWERS table, chapter 9, p100

questions.title: Mature eggs drive schistosomiasis pathology
questions.question: The pathological changes in Schistosomiasis are caused mainly by?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Immature eggs, not yet containing a fully developed miracidium, provoke a much weaker antigenic and granulomatous response than mature eggs.
explanations.B: Correct. It is specifically the mature egg, containing a live miracidium that continuously secretes antigens through microscopic pores in its shell, that provokes the granulomatous reaction responsible for most of schistosomiasis's pathology. Once an egg dies or calcifies, the inflammatory response around it also subsides.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adult worms are comparatively well tolerated by the host immune system and are not the main driver of chronic pathology.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cercariae are the free-swimming, skin-penetrating stage; beyond a possible early dermatitis, they are not the stage responsible for schistosomiasis's chronic pathology.

questions.learning_objective: State that mature eggs, specifically, are the main driver of schistosomiasis pathology.

questions.title: Fasciola gigantica is the small-intestine EXCEPT
questions.question: Small intestine is the habitat of the following worms EXCEPT?

explanations.A: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Taenia solium's adult tapeworm lives in the small intestine.
explanations.B: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Ascaris lumbricoides lives in the small intestine.
explanations.C: Incorrect (true statement, not the EXCEPT). Heterophyes heterophyes lives in the small intestine.
explanations.D: Correct. This is the exception, so it is the EXCEPT answer. Fasciola gigantica does not live in the small intestine; as a liver fluke, its adult habitat is the large bile ducts, unlike the three genuinely intestinal worms listed alongside it.

questions.learning_objective: Identify Fasciola gigantica as the exception to a small-intestinal habitat among the worms listed.

questions.title: Heterophyes reservoir hosts are fish-eating animals
questions.question: Reservoir hosts for Heterophyes are?

explanations.A: Correct. Fish-eating mammals such as dogs and cats serve as reservoir hosts for Heterophyes heterophyes. They become infected by eating the same raw or undercooked brackish-water fish that transmits the parasite to humans. By continuing to pass eggs in their own faeces, these animals help maintain transmission in endemic areas.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Herbivorous animals such as sheep and cattle are reservoir hosts for Fasciola, which they acquire by grazing on metacercaria-contaminated vegetation, not for Heterophyes heterophyes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Birds are not the standard reservoir hosts described for Heterophyes heterophyes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Frogs are not the standard reservoir hosts described for Heterophyes heterophyes.

questions.learning_objective: Identify fish-eating animals (dogs and cats) as reservoir hosts for Heterophyes heterophyes.

questions.title: Schistosoma infective stage is the furcocercous cercaria
questions.question: The infective stage of Schistosoma is?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A lophocercous cercaria is not Schistosoma's cercarial type.
explanations.B: Correct. The furcocercous (fork-tailed) cercaria is both the infective and the transmissible stage of Schistosoma. It swims freely in water and penetrates intact human skin directly, without ever encysting as a metacercaria, unlike the ingestion-route trematodes covered elsewhere in this chapter.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Schistosoma has no encysted metacercarial stage at all -- its cercaria penetrates skin directly, unlike Fasciola or Heterophyes heterophyes, which do encyst as metacercariae.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A leptocercous (simple-tailed) cercaria is the type produced by Fasciola-type flukes, not Schistosoma.

questions.learning_objective: State that the furcocercous cercaria is the infective stage of Schistosoma.

questions.title: S. haematobium lives in urinary bladder venules
questions.question: Schistosoma haematobium lives mainly in the venules of?

explanations.A: Correct. Schistosoma haematobium adult worms live mainly in the venous plexus of the urinary bladder wall (the vesical venous plexus). This is where the female deposits her terminal-spined eggs, which then work their way through the bladder wall into the urine.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The venules of the small intestine are not Schistosoma haematobium's habitat; it favours the vesical venous plexus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The venules of the stomach are not Schistosoma haematobium's habitat.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The venules of the large intestine are the habitat of Schistosoma mansoni, not Schistosoma haematobium.

questions.learning_objective: State that Schistosoma haematobium lives mainly in the venules of the urinary bladder.

questions.title: Trematode attachment organs are suckers
questions.question: Trematodes are characterized by?

options.A: Flattened dorsoventrally, bilaterally symmetrical and segmented

explanations.A: Incorrect (mixes a true and a false claim). Trematodes are indeed dorsoventrally flattened and bilaterally symmetrical, but they are unsegmented, unlike the segmented cestodes, so this statement as a whole is false.
explanations.B: Correct. Trematodes' organs of attachment are suckers -- typically an oral sucker around the mouth and a ventral sucker (acetabulum). They use these suckers to attach to and move along host tissue. This contrasts with the hooks or grooved bothria that some cestodes use instead.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trematodes do have a digestive system, though an incomplete one (a blind-ending gut with no anus); they are not without a digestive system altogether.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Most trematodes are hermaphroditic, not separately sexed; Schistosoma is the tested exception, not the rule.

questions.learning_objective: State that trematodes' organs of attachment are suckers.

questions.title: Schistosoma inhabits the portal vein
questions.question: which of the following trematodes inhibit the portal vein?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fasciola's adult habitat is the large bile ducts of the liver, not the portal vein.
explanations.B: Correct. Schistosoma worms mature in, and largely reside within, the portal venous system before migrating against portal blood flow to their species-specific final site (the mesenteric venules for S. mansoni, the vesical venous plexus for S. haematobium).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Heterophyes heterophyes' adult habitat is the small intestine, not the portal vein.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Paragonimus westermani's adult habitat is the lung, not the portal vein.

questions.learning_objective: State that adult Schistosoma worms reside in the portal venous system.

questions.title: S. mansoni deposits eggs in large intestinal venules
questions.question: The Schistosoma mansoni deposit their eggs?

options.A: Small venules in Small intestinal wall
options.B: Small venules in large intestinal wall

explanations.A: Incorrect. Small venules of the small intestinal wall are not where Schistosoma mansoni deposits its eggs.
explanations.B: Correct. Schistosoma mansoni deposits its lateral-spined eggs in the small venules of the large intestinal (colonic) wall. The eggs then work their way through the bowel wall to be excreted in stool, and eggs that instead embolise to the liver drive the periportal fibrosis of hepatosplenic schistosomiasis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Small venules of the bladder wall are where Schistosoma haematobium deposits its eggs, not Schistosoma mansoni.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Small venules of the biliary tracts are not where Schistosoma mansoni deposits its eggs; the biliary tree is instead Fasciola's habitat.

questions.learning_objective: State that Schistosoma mansoni deposits its eggs in the venules of the large intestinal wall.

questions.title: S. haematobium deposits eggs in bladder venules
questions.question: The Schistosoma haematobium deposlt their eggs?

options.A: Small venules in Small intestinal wall
options.B: Small venules in large intestinal wall

explanations.A: Incorrect. Small venules of the small intestinal wall are not where Schistosoma haematobium deposits its eggs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Small venules of the large intestinal wall are where Schistosoma mansoni deposits its eggs, not Schistosoma haematobium.
explanations.C: Correct. Schistosoma haematobium deposits its eggs in the small venules of the urinary bladder wall. The terminal-spined eggs then work their way through the bladder wall to be excreted in urine, and the resulting granulomatous reaction underlies urinary schistosomiasis's characteristic haematuria and, over time, bladder pathology.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Small venules of the biliary tracts are not where Schistosoma haematobium deposits its eggs; the biliary tree is instead Fasciola's habitat.

questions.learning_objective: State that Schistosoma haematobium deposits its eggs in the venules of the bladder wall.
